# Waypoint's invariants

The promises in `AGENTS.md`'s "Waypoint's promises", numbered, each with the checks that already hold it. The second review checks every one a risky pull request touches: a positive and a negative test per invariant touched, and any weakening of a check named here is blocking unless the linked issue asked for it. The full wording, with every exception, is in `AGENTS.md`; this list names the checks.

1. **Email stays on the server.** A message is read in memory for its booking; what is stored is the booking's fields, its Gmail id and, while something needs it, its subject, sender's domain and day, capped text and allowlisted markup, encrypted with `WAYPOINT_SECRET_KEY` (`storage/stored_mail.py`), deleted with its item, booking or mailbox. The scan's summary and every log line are counts, never a subject, sender or text. Held by: `tests/privacy.py`'s `no_leaks` around every test that reads mail (canary values in the body, the image bytes and the image addresses), `tests/test_hostile_markup.py` and `frontend/src/lib/email-render.test.ts` (the corpus in `tests/hostile_markup.py` comes out of the cleaner and the inline renderer inert), `tests/test_review_push.py` (a push after a scan carries counts only), Semgrep's `waypoint-mail-image-fetch` (image downloads only in `providers/mailimages.py`), the Semgrep rules that keep a message's body (`payload`, `raw`, decoded parts) in `domain/mail/extract.py` and decrypting in the storage layer, and Google's hosts only in `providers/gmail.py`.
2. **Email reaches an AI only when the household chose it.** Mail code gets its AI config only from `ai.mail_config`, which is `None` unless the AI is Local (Ollama); a hosted provider (OpenRouter) never gets email text; a scan sends a message only with "Read unreadable mail with AI automatically" on as well; an assistant over `/mcp` gets a message's text only on a connection granted the `mail` scope. Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-mail-ai-local-only`, `tests/test_mail_ai.py` (`HostedModeTests`: with OpenRouter no request reaches any AI host), `tests/test_mail_ai_auto.py` (a scan asks only with both switches on), `tests/test_mail_ai_dismiss.py` (only a `not_a_booking` answer dismisses, and only that one item), `tests/test_trip_destination.py` (the destination prompt is redacted of codes, names, addresses and numbers), and `tests/test_mcp_routes.py` and `tests/test_mcp_review.py` (the two routes that return email text need `mail`; without it an item is its parsed fields only).
3. **A kept message and its images are shown only to those who can see its item or booking.** The message and image routes, `GET /api/segments/{id}/code` (a parking booking's gate code, sealed in `segment_codes`) and `GET /api/offline` answer 404 to anyone else and are blocked for assistants; the offline copy holds no images and no gate code. Held by: `tests/test_offline.py` (canary values in `GET /api/offline`), `tests/test_gate_codes.py` (rule, follow-up, sealing, backup, deletion, visibility, `/mcp`, canaries), `tests/test_mcp_routes.py`, and `tests/test_every_route.py` (every route needs sign-in).
4. **You see the trips you're on.** A trip is visible to its people (everyone named on any of its bookings), to whoever booked it or one of its bookings, and to whoever got a confirmation for one in their own mailbox; nobody else, by any route, and a trip or segment you can't see is a 404, the same as one that doesn't exist. Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-trip-visibility` (no trip or segment query in `waypoint/server/` outside `domain/visibility.py`), `tests/test_trip_people.py` (a trip's people include everyone on its bookings), each route's 404 test for a trip you can't see, and the map's data read from disk with a stranger's 404 (`tests/test_geocode.py`, `tests/test_roads.py`, `tests/test_trip_roads.py`, `tests/test_states.py`, `tests/test_trip_states.py`). A trip's coordinates go to an outside service in one case only: the route replay's map, when a MapKit key is configured on the server and `WAYPOINT_MAPKIT_ENABLED` has not been turned off (on by default, inactive without a key; the Content-Security-Policy is widened only while it is active: `https://*.apple-mapkit.com` and `blob:` in `img-src`, `connect-src` and `worker-src`, and `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in `script-src`; the owner's decision on issue #530, with no household setting or per-trip exclusion). Then Apple's script is loaded from Apple's servers, is not pinned (it is Apple's auto-updating address, `https://cdn.apple-mapkit.com/mk/x/mapkit.js`, which Apple changes and browsers cache for minutes, so no integrity hash is possible) and runs in the page with the app's own access (the signed-in session's same-origin API, the trips and loyalty numbers on screen, the offline copy), so with MapKit active you are trusting Apple, not only sending it a viewport; Apple also learns the viewer's IP address and browser, the area on screen and that this Waypoint's address was the page's origin, and the exact start and end coordinates of each drive in the replay (a car leg, Home included; never a flight, cruise or train), which the browser sends to Apple's directions service to trace the route along roads (a failed call keeps the bundled line; the owner's decision, issue #630); the server only signs a short-lived token (`GET /api/mapkit/token`, sign-in required, blocked for assistants, the private key never returned or logged, the Key ID and Team ID never logged; the token itself carries them as `kid` and `iss`). With no key or the flag off nothing goes to Apple, the Content-Security-Policy names no Apple host and the replay is the SVG map, which any MapKit failure also falls back to. Held by: `tests/test_mapkit.py`, the MapKit Vitest suites and Semgrep's `waypoint-mapkit-hosts`.
5. **IDs are for the household.** Loyalty and Known Traveler numbers are visible to every signed-in member, encrypted at rest, masked until asked for, and never in logs, reports, notifications, hosted AI prompts or the browser's storage (the device's encrypted offline copy excepted, which never holds one). Held by: Semgrep (decrypting only in the storage layer, `oidc.py`, `domain/loyalty.py` and `providers/gmail.py`), ESLint (nothing kept in the browser's storage; the Cache API only in `frontend/src/lib/offline-vault.ts`), `tests/test_offline.py` (canary numbers never in `GET /api/offline`), `tests/test_loyalty.py`, and `no_leaks` in the tests.
6. **Times are where they happen.** A booking's times are wall-clock times at its airports or hotel, stored with the place's IANA zone; nothing converts them to the server's zone or UTC on the way; "today" and scheduled hours are the machine's local time, and anything that tells another system about a time carries the right zone. Held by: Semgrep (no naive `datetime.now()` in domain or provider code, no bare `date.today()` in background jobs and provider modules, no `datetime.utcnow()`; month arithmetic only in `waypoint/dates.py`), strict mypy over `domain/` and `providers/`, and `tests/test_dates.py`.
7. **Every route is held without a test of its own.** A new route needs sign-in, refuses a change without the app's header or from another site, has its reply typed in `waypoint/server/contract.py` and has a docs page. Held by: `tests/test_every_route.py`, `make api-contract-check` and `make feature-map-check` (every route has a test: `tools/feature_map_allowlist.txt` started empty and stays that way).
8. **Access ends with the person.** Every kind of session, grant, token, feed key or mailbox connection ends when its owner can no longer sign in, like browser sessions do. Held by: `oidc.access_lapsed`, and each kind's own test: `tests/test_hardening.py` (`test_removed_email_ends_sessions`), `tests/test_gmail.py` (a lapsed owner's mailbox connection is ended by the sweep, by listing mailboxes and even when Google can't be told), `tests/test_mcp_oauth.py` and `tests/test_mcp_oauth_http.py` (assistant connections), and `tests/test_reminders.py`. A new kind of credential needs a test like these; none of them covers it by itself.
9. **Nothing about the app leaves it.** Waypoint sends nothing about itself to any outside service (the MapKit case in invariant 4 is Apple's unpinned script running in the viewer's page, never the server sending trip data): no telemetry, error reporting or analytics SDKs, every log line through `monitoring.log`, and every outbound connection through `tls.urlopen` (or `tls.post_http2` for Apple's HTTP/2 push). Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-no-telemetry` and the `tls.urlopen` and `waypoint-raw-httpx` paved-path rules, ESLint (no `console.log`; `fetch(` only in `lib/api.ts`), and `no_leaks` (a canary in a request sent through `tls.urlopen` or `tls.post_http2` fails).
10. **Backups restore what was there.** A backup holds the encrypted message text and gate codes as they were, and `backup.restore` refuses one made at an older schema revision than the baseline with a message saying so. Held by: `tests/test_backup.py` and `tests/test_gate_codes.py`.
11. **The automation is checked the way the code is.** Workflows run bash with `-eo pipefail`, pin every action by SHA with its version in a comment, check out with `persist-credentials: false`, pass event values as environment variables, paginate `gh api` lists, and run on `vars.RUNS_ON` or say why they stay on GitHub's runners; the reviews and the merge gate run from main's copies, and the fleet workflows are pinned by commit at one version. Held by: the fleet checks' workflow conventions, zizmor in the security scans, and fleet's `sync.yml` (pins that disagree fail).
12. **Photos are shared by their person.** A photo reaches someone else only while its person's grant for that trip is active with the Trip scope, the viewer is one of the trip's people, and it is not excluded; every trip-facing reply, count, pin and image is built from the photos that one predicate (`photos.visible`) lets the viewer see, assistants included, and taking a photo back takes effect on the next request. The two intentional exceptions are person-only: Needs a look and its image routes use `photos.unsettled`, and the removed-photo thumbnail uses `photos.removed`. AGENTS.md "Photos are shared by their person" has the full text (cache headers, stream cut-off on removal, the Immich address and key never reaching the browser, the same 404 for every refusal). Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-photo-access` (no `Photo` query or insert in `waypoint/server/`, `waypoint/domain/` or `waypoint/storage/` outside `photos.py`, `photogrants.py` and `photosync.py`; `storage/models.py` and `storage/photo_sources.py` are scanned, the table mapping and the source counts carry a line-level `nosemgrep`, and so do the demo seed rows in `domain/demo.py`), `tests/test_photo_access.py`, `tests/test_photo_proxy.py` and `no_leaks` with canary asset ids and places.
